order: The review runner is inherently the driver for one cross-vendor engine, but the inert tier and the verification manifest are review policy and must bind every review path, including the in-session fallback the Director runs when that engine is unavailable, and any future engine. In the protocol document's section 8.3, reword the tier as policy, so whoever reviews verifies the inertness claim from the diff, the runner enforces it automatically for the engine it drives, and a fallback review applies exactly the same rule by hand; declare the manifest the canonical command set for every verifier. In section 5, make the fallback review inherit the full policy, verifying tier claims from the diff, judging the executor's pasted verification against the manifest, and recording the tier and depth actually run. Document the split between policy and transport in the README and in the runner header.
claims: All three sub-items landed, with the tier reworded as policy for whoever reviews and the manifest declared the canonical command set for every verifier. The fallback section now carries all three inherited obligations, verifying an inert-tier claim from the diff, judging pasted verification against the manifest, and recording the tier and depth actually run. The README and the runner header document the split. Grepping manifest across the changed files returns three hits, in the tier item, the fallback section, and the README.
